newsitem.title: LATVIA: S&P SAYS RIGA NEEDS TO KEEP FINANCE PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: S&P SAYS RIGA NEEDS TO KEEP FINANCE PERFORMANCE.

text.p: Riga city said on Wednesday that its Standard & Poors long-term BBB- rating may be upgraded if the capital city continues a strong financial performance and has low to moderate debt.

Riga earlier announced that S&P gave it an unchanged BBB- rating despite the city's request for a higher one although the outlook was changed from positive to stable. S&P also gave it an unchanged A3 short-term credit rating.

Riga city finance department deputy director for investment credit questions Inga Cerbule said an upgrade in the rating depended on a continuation of the city's strong financial performance and low-to-moderate debt levels despite the implementation of an extensive investment programme.
"The rating was supported by Riga's strong financial performance, low debt burden and healthy growth prospects, Standard & Poors say in their evaluation," Inga Cerbule told Reuters.
The rating agency also listed income and expenditure distribution uncertainties between the central government and municipalities and limited internal liquidity as the reason for an unchanged rating.
The existence of a fairly large shadow economy was also constraining the city's tax revenues, Cerbule quoted the agency as saying.
Riga is currently banned from taking loans under legislation but may borrow if the laws are changed.
